head: 24d60aef
gate: Stable HTTP/1 pull body reader with content decoding, HTTP/2 pull nextBody and concurrent stream serving aliases, HTTP/3 cumulative max_body_bytes for server requests and client response/push bodies

commands.http3_body_bound: zig build test-lib -Dtest-filter="HTTP/3 incremental reader" --summary all
commands.continuous_concurrent: zig build test-lib -Dtest-filter="HTTP/3 continuous concurrent" --summary all
commands.handshake_bounded_body: zig build test-lib -Dtest-filter="handshake concurrent serving bounds a large POST body" --summary all

notes: The HTTP/1 pull BodyReader drives the existing push parser through a bounded FIFO producer. Tests cover a 200 KiB body with 100-continue and keep-alive, chunked trailers, cancellation closing an unread connection, max_body_bytes rejection, non-blocking takeRequest, and Head.streamContentDecoder identity decoding. HTTP/2 ServerDuplexStream.nextBody pulls DATA, retains trailers for requestTrailers, returns null at END_STREAM, surfaces peer resets as StreamReset and exposes streamContentDecoder. HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 concurrent batch aliases are exposed through netz.streaming. HTTP/3 streaming readers enforce a cumulative Limits.max_body_bytes budget for server requests and for client response/push bodies, counting already-read DATA so a later frame cannot reset it; exceeding the budget surfaces error.PayloadTooLarge at the next read boundary. `serveConcurrentStreams` on HTTP/2 Connection and HTTP/3 HandshakeServerSession accepts streams continuously, runs one handler task per stream up to max_streams, serializes body reads and response head/DATA/trailers/reset through the connection owner, supports streaming responses and response trailers on both HTTP/3 server types, and stops on shutdown/deadline/idle timeout with GOAWAY. The HTTP/2 continuous test multiplexes two streams on one connection with concurrent handlers. HTTP/3 request DATA is copied into a per-stream buffer capped by max_stream_buffer (or max_buffered_body_bytes) with owner-side backpressure; the total body remains bounded by max_body_bytes. Suppress-body HEAD/204/304 responses finish without DATA, and finishWithTrailers ends the stream after the final DATA. Peer cancellation is delivered to nextBody as error.StreamReset and is covered by a deterministic loopback test. HEAD responses with representation Content-Length finish from startResponse without DATA, and a handler may return without calling finish. HandshakeServerSession availableRequestData maps a consumed DATA frame to zero bytes instead of UnexpectedFrame, so non-empty POST bodies stream through the same engine. A handshake concurrent test with the adapter default cap (HandshakeSessionOptions.max_stream_buffer = 1400, no per-call override) streams a 2048-byte POST in 16-byte handler reads; when the resident queue fills, the owner wakes the handler to drain it before resuming the reader. Without that wake the handler deadlocked until its deadline and the owner reset a correct stream. HandshakeSessionOptions.max_stream_buffer must still admit the largest incoming QUIC STREAM frame, so the test lowers the client's max_stream_frame_data to 512.
